elements.element: Customer has no minimum purchase or take-or-pay commitment.
elements.evidence: The clause states that Customer commits to purchase “no minimum amount” and removes the original take-or-pay obligation.

elements.element: Customer pays fees only for Services that Customer orders or uses.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly provides that Customer “pays only for Services ordered or used.”

elements.element: If a purchase commitment applies, it is limited to the current 12-month term.
elements.evidence: No nonzero purchase commitment applies, so there is no commitment extending beyond 12 months. The residual reference to the next three years imposes no minimum-volume obligation.

elements.element: If a purchase commitment applies, Customer may reduce it on 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The clause imposes no purchase commitment requiring reduction, so the condition for this protection is demonstrably absent.

elements.element: If Customer has a commitment shortfall, it is addressed through a true-up rather than a penalty.
elements.evidence: Because there is no minimum commitment, no commitment shortfall or associated penalty can arise; payment is limited to Services ordered or used.

result.reason: The operative redline reaches the preferred position by eliminating the minimum and take-or-pay obligation and limiting payment to ordered or used Services. It also provides protection exceeding the fallback because no commitment exists to require a term limit, reduction right, or shortfall remedy. The edit is substantively effective and does not add unrelated terms, but drafting quality is reduced by the awkward and unnecessary phrase “commits to purchase no minimum amount ... in each of the next three years,” which should ideally be replaced with a direct statement that Customer has no minimum purchase commitment.
